audit_items.title: Does the EL node correctly extract and order deposit data from matching logs according to receipt_keys sequence?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: For all logs L in receipt where L.address == DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS AND L.topics[0] == depositTopic: extract_deposit_data(L) must be called in receipt order, and results concatenated into reqData preserving that order.
preconditions: logs is valid array of Log pointers
postconditions: Returned FlatRequest contains deposit data ordered by receipt appearance
Error returned if any log unpacking fails
invariants: Deposit data length must be DepositRequestDataLen (192 bytes) per deposit

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: ParseDepositLogs iterates through logs sequentially. For each log matching contract address and topic, it calls unpackDepositLog which validates log data structure via validateDepositLog (checking exact 576 byte length and correct ABI offsets), then extracts fields. Data is appended to reqData in iteration order.
potential_issues: validateDepositLog uses uint256 for offset parsing - safe from overflow
Fixed offset validation ensures canonical layout

phase3_findings.rationale: The implementation correctly iterates logs in order and validates deposit data structure before extraction. The validateDepositLog function enforces exact byte offsets preventing malformed data. Order preservation is guaranteed by sequential append.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does block validation reject blocks where trie_get returns None for any key in receipt_keys?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: For block validation: compute receipt_hash = DeriveSha(receipts) and verify receipt_hash == header.ReceiptHash. Any missing receipt causes hash mismatch leading to block rejection.
postconditions: Block rejected if receipt hash mismatch
No partial state changes on rejection
invariants: Receipt hash in header must match computed hash from receipts

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: ValidateReceipts computes receiptHash via types.DeriveSha(receipts) and compares against header.ReceiptHash. Mismatch returns error. The trie derivation ensures all receipts are accounted for - missing receipt would cause different root hash.
potential_issues: Receipt hash validation is atomic - all or nothing
No explicit trie_get - uses hash comparison instead

phase3_findings.rationale: While implementation doesn't use explicit trie_get, the receipt hash verification achieves equivalent security - any missing or modified receipt causes hash mismatch and block rejection.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node properly validate receipts trie consistency before processing blocks from untrusted block producers?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Block validation MUST verify: DeriveSha(receipts) == header.ReceiptHash before accepting block.
preconditions: Block received from P2P or local production
postconditions: Valid blocks have consistent receipt trie

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: core/blockchain.go:411-422 computes receiptHash and compares with header. Validation occurs before block is persisted or state modified.

phase3_findings.rationale: Receipt trie validation is performed atomically before block acceptance. Implementation matches specification requirements.

audit_items.title: Can a malicious block producer cause a network split by crafting blocks with inconsistent receipts trie?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: All honest nodes MUST consistently reject blocks where receipt trie root doesn't match header.ReceiptHash.
postconditions: Malicious block rejected by all honest nodes

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Receipt hash computation uses types.DeriveSha which is deterministic. All nodes using this implementation will compute identical hashes for identical receipt sets.

phase3_findings.rationale: Within Erigon, receipt validation is deterministic. Cross-client consistency depends on spec compliance but this codebase implements correctly.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Does compute_requests_hash correctly implement double-SHA-256 construction?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: requests_hash = sha256(sha256(r1) || sha256(r2) || ... || sha256(rn)) where ri are individual requests.
preconditions: executionRequests is valid slice of byte arrays
invariants: Order of requests affects final hash

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: ComputeExecutionRequestHash creates sha256.New(), iterates requests computing sha256.Sum256(r) for each, writes digest to outer hasher, returns final hash. This is correct double-SHA-256 construction.
potential_issues: Empty list case returns sha256() of empty input which is valid per spec

phase3_findings.rationale: Implementation correctly implements double-SHA-256: inner hash per request, outer hash over concatenated digests. Matches EIP-7685 specification.

audit_items.title: Verify EL Node implements consistent double-SHA-256 request hashing across all code paths

phase1_specification.formal_specification: All code paths invoking request hash computation MUST use identical double-SHA-256 construction.
postconditions: Consistent hash output across all paths

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Found 2 call sites: block_collector.go:184 and execution_client_direct.go:64. Both call cltypes.ComputeExecutionRequestHash - single implementation ensures consistency.

phase3_findings.rationale: Single implementation of ComputeExecutionRequestHash used across codebase. No alternative paths found.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Is request ordering in compute_requests_hash deterministic and consistent across EL/CL boundary?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Request ordering in hash computation MUST match input order. No sorting or reordering during computation.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: for _, r := range executionRequests iterates in slice order. sha.Write preserves order of writes. No sorting applied.
edge_cases_identified: Go range iteration is deterministic for slices

phase3_findings.rationale: Go slice iteration is deterministic. No sorting or reordering operations. Input order directly determines hash output.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node maintain request list order when building the requests hash?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: EL node MUST maintain request insertion order through hash computation.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: ComputeExecutionRequestHash processes requests in slice order. Upstream accumulation in execution/consensus/merge/merge.go appends in processing order.

phase3_findings.rationale: Order preservation confirmed through data flow analysis. No sorting operations between accumulation and hash computation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Does compute_requests_hash return the correct SHA256 digest for an empty requests list?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: compute_requests_hash([]) == sha256() == e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: With empty slice, loop body never executes. sha.Sum(nil) returns hash of empty data written to hasher (nothing), which equals SHA256 of empty input.
edge_cases_identified: nil slice vs empty slice - both work correctly
potential_issues: None - Go sha256.New().Sum(nil) correctly returns empty hash

phase3_findings.rationale: Empty input handling is correct. sha256.New() with no writes returns expected empty-input hash.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node correctly handle blocks with zero deposit requests when computing the requests hash?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Blocks with no deposit events MUST have deposit request component as empty. Hash computation handles empty case.
preconditions: Block with no deposit contract events

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: ParseDepositLogs returns nil, nil when no matching logs found (lines 133-136). Upstream handles nil appropriately.

phase3_findings.rationale: Empty deposit handling is correct. nil return signals no deposits, which is valid.

audit_items.title: Does the CL node correctly validate blocks with empty requests lists received from EL nodes?
audit_items.skip_reason: CL Node (actor-cl-node) check - this codebase is an EL (Execution Layer) client.

audit_items.title: Is the RLP encoding field order invariant (nonce, balance, storage_root, keccak256(code)) strictly enforced in encode_account?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Account RLP encoding MUST follow order: nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash. This is Ethereum Yellow Paper specification.
postconditions: RLP output in canonical field order

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Account encoding in erigon-lib uses custom compact encoding for storage efficiency, not standard RLP. The encoding order is: nonce_len, balance_len, incarnation_len, code_hash presence flag, then values.
edge_cases_identified: Storage encoding is compact, not standard RLP
potential_issues: Storage encoding is non-standard but internally consistent

phase3_findings.rationale: Erigon uses custom storage encoding. For consensus-critical paths (state root computation), proper RLP encoding is used elsewhere. Internal storage format is consistent.

audit_items.title: Can the encode_account function be made to use raw account code instead of its keccak256 hash during RLP encoding?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Account RLP MUST contain keccak256(code), never raw code. Raw code stored separately.
postconditions: Only CodeHash (32 bytes) in encoded account
invariants: Code and CodeHash are separate storage concerns

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Account struct contains CodeHash [32]byte field, not raw code. Encoding functions use CodeHash directly. Code is stored/retrieved separately via code hash lookups.

phase3_findings.rationale: Type system prevents raw code in account encoding. CodeHash field is fixed 32-byte array.

audit_items.title: Can the EMPTY_ACCOUNT constant be mutated or replaced after module initialization?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Empty account representation MUST be immutable after initialization.
invariants: nonce=0, balance=0, code=empty hash, storage=empty root

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Go doesn't have frozen objects. NewAccount() creates new instances. Empty account detection done via field value checks, not identity comparison.
potential_issues: Go allows mutation of any struct, but code patterns prevent misuse

phase3_findings.rationale: While Go lacks immutability guarantees, empty account detection uses value comparison. No mutable global empty account constant found.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Are Address values with length != 20 bytes rejected at P2P message validation layer?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Address type MUST be exactly 20 bytes. RLP decoding MUST reject non-20-byte addresses.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Address is defined as [length.Addr]byte where length.Addr=20. Fixed-size array in Go inherently enforces length. RLP decoding via DecodeRLP checks byte length explicitly (e.g., set_code_tx.go:254-255 checks len(b)!=20).
potential_issues: Type system provides guarantee at compile time for internal use

phase3_findings.rationale: Address is fixed 20-byte array type. RLP decoding includes explicit length checks before assignment.

audit_items.title: Does the RLP decoding layer enforce exactly 20 bytes for Address type during deserialization?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: RLP decoder MUST reject addresses not exactly 20 bytes.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: set_code_tx.go:254-256 explicitly checks if len(b) != 20 and returns error. Similar checks in other transaction types. Address type [20]byte enforces at assignment.

phase3_findings.rationale: Explicit length check in RLP decoding: if len(b) != 20 { return fmt.Errorf(...) }

audit_items.title: Can a malicious P2P peer cause state corruption by sending transactions with invalid Address lengths?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Invalid address length in P2P message MUST cause message rejection, not state corruption.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: RLP decoding returns error on invalid length (line 255). Error propagates up, transaction rejected. No partial decoding state persisted on error.
potential_issues: None - early validation, clean error path

phase3_findings.rationale: RLP decoding validates before creating transaction object. Error path is clean with no partial state.

audit_items.title: Is the Address length invariant consistently enforced across all block fields containing addresses?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: All address fields in block/transaction structures MUST use Address type enforcing 20 bytes.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Address type is common.Address = [20]byte throughout codebase. Transaction To, From, contract addresses all use this type. Header Coinbase uses common.Address.

phase3_findings.rationale: Address type consistently used across block and transaction fields. Fixed-size array enforces length at compile time.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Are Root and VersionedHash values validated to be exactly 32 bytes during P2P message deserialization?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Hash/Root types MUST be exactly 32 bytes. RLP decoding MUST reject non-32-byte values.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Hash type is [32]byte fixed array. RLP decoding for hashes uses rlp.Stream methods that validate length. VersionedHash in blob transactions also 32 bytes.
potential_issues: None - fixed array type + RLP validation

phase3_findings.rationale: Hash32 types are [32]byte arrays. RLP stream methods validate byte lengths during decoding.

audit_items.title: Does the P2P peer message handler enforce strict 32-byte length checks on all hash fields before forwarding to execution layer?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: All hash fields validated to 32 bytes at P2P layer.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Hash = [32]byte is used throughout. P2P message decoding uses RLP which validates lengths. DevP2P protocol handlers use typed structures with Hash fields.
edge_cases_identified: All hash fields use common.Hash type

phase3_findings.rationale: Fixed-size Hash type used consistently. RLP decoding validates before assigning to typed fields.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node reject blocks containing Root or VersionedHash values with incorrect lengths received from P2P peers?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Block import MUST reject blocks with incorrectly sized root/hash fields.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Header fields like StateRoot, TxHash, ReceiptHash are common.Hash = [32]byte. RLP decoding validates lengths. Blob versioned hashes also validated during transaction decode.

phase3_findings.rationale: All root/hash fields use fixed [32]byte type. RLP layer validates before struct assignment.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is Bloom filter size (256 bytes) strictly enforced during P2P message deserialization?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Bloom filter MUST be exactly 256 bytes (2048 bits).

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Bloom = [BloomByteLength]byte = [256]byte. Fixed array type. RLP decoding validates length when assigning to typed Bloom field.

phase3_findings.rationale: Bloom type is fixed [256]byte array. Type system enforces size at compile time and RLP validates at runtime.

audit_items.title: Does the P2P peer message validation layer reject blocks with malformed Bloom filters before processing?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Invalid bloom size causes immediate P2P message rejection.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Header Bloom field is types.Bloom = [256]byte. RLP decoding rejects mismatched sizes before header struct is fully constructed.

phase3_findings.rationale: Fixed-size Bloom type with RLP validation ensures early rejection of malformed data.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node properly validate Bloom filter size invariant to prevent consensus divergence?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Computed bloom must match header bloom. Size enforced by type.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: core/blockchain.go:178-180 computes CreateBloom(receipts) and compares with header.Bloom. Both are [256]byte types. Mismatch returns error.

phase3_findings.rationale: Bloom validation combines type-level size guarantee with value comparison against computed bloom.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is the EIP-7702 Authorization tuple strictly validated to contain exactly the required 6 fields?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Authorization tuple: (chain_id, address, nonce, y_parity, r, s) - exactly 6 fields.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Authorization struct has exactly 6 fields: ChainID, Address, Nonce, YParity, R, S. RLP decoding in decodeAuthorizations validates list structure.
potential_issues: RLP list decoding validates field count

phase3_findings.rationale: Authorization struct exactly mirrors EIP-7702 spec. RLP decoding validates against struct fields.

audit_items.title: Does the EL Node correctly reject Authorization tuples with incorrect field count during RLP parsing?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: RLP parser MUST reject authorization with != 6 fields.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: RLP stream decoding expects specific sequence of types. Missing fields cause decode error. Extra fields detected by ListEnd() mismatch.

phase3_findings.rationale: RLP stream decoding is strict - wrong field count or types cause immediate error.

audit_items.title: Is the EIP-7702 Authorizer protected against signature verification failures caused by malformed Authorization field types?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Invalid y_parity, r, s values MUST cause graceful verification failure, not crash.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: ToAuthorization validates: yParity < 256, r fits 256 bits, s fits 256 bits. Returns error on overflow. Signature verification happens after field validation.

phase3_findings.rationale: Field validation with explicit overflow checks. Error path returns cleanly without panic.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is ALL data received from P2P peers fully validated before processing?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: All P2P data MUST pass RLP validation and type checks before state processing.
postconditions: Only valid data reaches state logic

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: P2P messages decoded via RLP into typed structs. Type system enforces field constraints. Additional semantic validation in consensus rules.
edge_cases_identified: Various data types require different validation

phase3_findings.rationale: Multi-layer validation: RLP structure -> Type constraints -> Consensus rules. Comprehensive but complex.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node have comprehensive validation for all P2P-received data types before state transitions?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Complete validation chain before state modification.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Data flow: P2P -> RLP decode -> Type validation -> Consensus validation -> State transition. Each layer adds checks.
potential_issues: Large attack surface but layered defense

phase3_findings.rationale: Layered validation architecture. Each component validates its inputs.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is RLP-encoded account data from P2P peers validated against size constraints before parsing?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: RLP decoder MUST enforce size limits before allocation.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: RLP decoder reads length prefixes and validates against available data. Go's memory allocator provides some protection. Erigon uses streaming RLP decoder which limits memory impact.
potential_issues: Large declared sizes should be bounded

phase3_findings.rationale: Streaming RLP decoder + Go memory safety. Protocol-level limits on block/transaction sizes provide defense.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node properly reject malformed RLP data from untrusted P2P peers without excessive resource consumption?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Malformed RLP rejection MUST be resource-bounded.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: RLP decoder validates structure incrementally. Early exit on errors. No full data buffering before validation.

phase3_findings.rationale: Streaming RLP decoder with early exit on errors. Resource consumption bounded by stream read limits.

audit_items.title: Are there pre-allocation limits enforced in the RLP decoder to prevent memory exhaustion attacks?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: RLP decoder MUST limit pre-allocation sizes.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: RLP decoder validates declared sizes against actual data availability. Protocol limits (block gas, tx size) provide upper bounds. Go runtime provides additional memory protection.

phase3_findings.rationale: Multiple defense layers: RLP size validation, protocol limits, Go runtime. No unbounded allocations from untrusted sizes.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is per-deposit-event CPU cost in extract_deposit_data bounded to prevent DoS?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Per-deposit processing MUST have bounded CPU cost.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: unpackDepositLog: validateDepositLog O(1) checks, ABI unpack O(n) where n=data size (fixed 576), byte copies O(1). Total: O(1) per deposit.

phase3_findings.rationale: Deposit processing is O(1) per event. Total cost scales linearly with deposit count, which is gas-bounded.

audit_items.title: Does the P2P peer enforce rate limiting or early rejection of blocks with excessive deposit events?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Blocks exceeding deposit limits should be rejected.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Deposit count bounded by block gas limit. No explicit deposit count check, but gas validation ensures bounded processing.

phase3_findings.rationale: Gas limits implicitly bound deposit count. Explicit count validation could add defense-in-depth.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node maintain acceptable block processing throughput at maximum deposit event capacity?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Block processing time MUST remain acceptable at max deposit load.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: O(1) per deposit with O(n) total. Pre-allocated slice reduces allocations. No expensive operations per deposit.

phase3_findings.rationale: Linear processing with pre-allocation. Gas limits bound maximum deposits, keeping processing time acceptable.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002/tb-003: Is malformed deposit event data from DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS properly detected and does it cause block rejection?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Malformed deposit log data MUST cause block rejection.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: validateDepositLog checks: exact 576 byte length, correct ABI offsets (160,256,320,384,512), correct field sizes (48,32,8,96,8). Any mismatch returns InvalidDepositLogErr.

phase3_findings.rationale: Strict validation of deposit log structure. Any deviation causes block rejection with clear error.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Is Uint.from_be_bytes offset parsing protected against integer overflow in fixed-width implementations?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Offset parsing MUST not overflow in fixed-width implementations.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Uses uint256.NewInt(0).SetBytes() which is arbitrary precision. CmpUint64() compares against fixed values. No overflow possible with uint256.

phase3_findings.rationale: uint256 library provides arbitrary precision integers. Comparison against fixed constants is safe.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node properly validate deposit data offsets before extracting and processing deposit information?

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: validateDepositLog checks exact offset values: 160, 256, 320, 384, 512. Any different value causes rejection. This ensures canonical ABI encoding.
potential_issues: None - exact value matching prevents malicious offsets

phase3_findings.rationale: Exact offset validation. No arithmetic on offsets - just comparison. Prevents offset manipulation attacks.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Is compute_requests_hash deterministic across all execution paths and thread contexts?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Function MUST be deterministic - same input always produces same output.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: sha256.New() creates new instance per call. No global state used. sha256.Sum256() is deterministic. Slice iteration order is deterministic in Go.
potential_issues: None - pure function with no shared state

phase3_findings.rationale: Pure function with no side effects. sha256 is deterministic. No thread-local or global mutable state.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node produce identical requests hash outputs for identical block data across restarts and different instances?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Hash output MUST be identical across restarts and instances.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Function has no state dependencies. SHA256 is standard algorithm. No randomness or timing dependencies. Go's sha256 implementation is deterministic.

phase3_findings.rationale: Stateless function using standardized SHA256. Identical output guaranteed across restarts and instances.

phase1_specification.formal_specification: All buffer reads MUST be bounds-checked before access.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: validateDepositLog checks len(data) == 576 first. All subsequent slice operations use fixed indices within this known length. Go panics on out-of-bounds, but validation prevents reaching that code with invalid lengths.

phase3_findings.rationale: Length validation (line 65-67) ensures all subsequent slice operations (data[0:32], etc.) are within bounds.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node maintain memory safety invariants when processing untrusted deposit data from external sources?

phase1_specification.formal_specification: Memory safety MUST be maintained for all untrusted inputs.

phase2_code_analysis.implementation_summary: Go provides memory safety (bounds checking, no buffer overflows). validateDepositLog adds application-level validation. ABI unpacking uses safe library functions.

phase3_findings.rationale: Go's memory safety combined with explicit length validation ensures no memory corruption from malicious inputs.
